title: Spark — Everything
description: Every reading from one DGX Spark: GPU, CPU, unified memory, NVMe, network, RoCE, thermals, containers, databases, systemd and kernel.

panels.title: Power cuts
panels.description: Shutdowns the SSD was not warned about, over its whole life: power cuts and hard resets.

panels.title: Host guard
panels.description: The packet filter that keeps model and exporter ports off the office LAN.

panels.title: GPU busy
panels.description: Share of time a kernel was executing. The worker rank spins, so this can read 95 % while nothing useful happens: read it with power.

panels.title: Busy by process
panels.description: Which process the busy share belongs to.

panels.title: GPU memory by owner
panels.description: Unified memory held by CUDA contexts, attributed to containers.

panels.title: Throttling
panels.description: The hardware's own explanation for a slowdown.

panels.title: By mode
panels.description: iowait high with user low means the CPU is waiting on disk, not busy.

panels.title: Every core
panels.description: This SoC has ten fast cores at 3.9 GHz and ten efficient ones at 2.8 GHz. A single hot line is a single-threaded bottleneck the average hides.

panels.title: Waiting for CPU
panels.description: PSI: share of time at least one task wanted a CPU and did not get it.

panels.title: Top processes by CPU
panels.description: Grouped by process name. In cores.

panels.title: Top processes by memory
panels.description: Shared memory counts once per process, so PostgreSQL reads high. GPU memory is not in these figures on this hardware.

panels.title: Unified memory: shared between the CPU and the GPU
Where the memory is
panels.description: GPU memory is not in any process's resident size on this hardware, so model weights show up as the remainder.

targets.expr: node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{node="$node"} - node_memory_MemFree_bytes{node="$node"} - node_memory_Cached_bytes{node="$node"} - node_memory_Buffers_bytes{node="$node"} - node_memory_AnonPages_bytes{node="$node"} - node_memory_Slab_bytes{node="$node"} - node_memory_PageTables_bytes{node="$node"} - node_memory_KernelStack_bytes{node="$node"}

panels.title: Swap
panels.description: When swap is full, the next shortfall goes straight to the OOM killer.

panels.title: Swap traffic
panels.description: Pages per second.

panels.title: Pressure
panels.description: PSI. All tasks stalled on memory is time the machine did no work at all.

panels.title: Major page faults
panels.description: A fault that has to go to disk.

panels.title: SSD life used
panels.description: The vendor's estimate. It can pass 100 %; data is not lost at that point, but the warranty is.

panels.title: Powered on
panels.description: The drive's own count. The NVMe specification lets it leave out time in low-power states, so it runs far behind the calendar.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Average time per completed operation.

panels.title: SSD writes per day
panels.description: What wears the drive. Swap traffic lands here.

panels.title: Interfaces
panels.description: Docker's veths and bridges are left out; per-container traffic is on the Containers page.

panels.title: Clock offset
panels.description: Timing-sensitive tests fail on the worker past about 40 ms.

panels.title: Connection tracking
panels.description: At 100 % the kernel starts dropping new connections, Docker's included.

panels.title: Throughput by rail
panels.description: From the InfiniBand counters. RDMA traffic never touches the kernel network stack, so netdev counters read flat zero on a healthy fabric. The split between rails is uneven by design.

panels.title: Retransmits and sequence errors
panels.description: From the NIC itself. Zero on a healthy fabric. These rise before throughput falls.

panels.title: Congestion
panels.description: Congestion notifications. On a direct cable between two Sparks these should stay at zero.

panels.title: Errors
panels.description: A peer dying also makes the transport counters move once.

panels.title: Every sensor
panels.description: The ACPI zones are not labelled by the firmware, so they cannot be tied to a component. NVMe and ConnectX are.

panels.title: Containers
panels.description: Blank GPU memory means none. Blank network means the container shares the host's network, so its traffic cannot be told apart. Exited containers are listed with their status.

targets.expr: max by (node, container, project, image, status) (spark_container_info{node="$node"})
max by (node, container) (time() - spark_container_started_timestamp_seconds{node="$node"} and on (node, container) spark_container_running == 1)

panels.title: CPU by container
panels.description: In cores. The ten busiest.

panels.title: Memory by container
panels.description: Working set, excluding GPU memory. The ten largest.

panels.title: Swap by container
panels.description: Who has been pushed out to disk.

panels.title: All databases
panels.description: Found automatically on every Spark. Status, version, connections, CPU, memory and disk need no login. Detail says what else is known: `login` means full statistics, `info` means the engine answers without one, `liveness` means no credentials are in use for this project. Blank means not measured, not zero.

targets.expr: max by (node, container, engine, project, version, stats) (spark_db_info{node="$node"})
100 * sum by (node, container) (rate(spark_db_cache_reads_total{node="$node",source="hit"}[5m])) / sum by (node, container) (rate(spark_db_cache_reads_total{node="$node"}[5m]) > 0)
sum by (node, container) (rate(spark_container_cpu_seconds_total[2m]) and on (node, container) spark_db_up{node="$node"})
max by (node, container) (spark_container_memory_working_set_bytes and on (node, container) spark_db_up{node="$node"})
max by (node, container) (spark_container_memory_swap_bytes and on (node, container) spark_db_up{node="$node"})
sum by (node, container) (rate(spark_container_disk_written_bytes_total[2m]) and on (node, container) spark_db_up{node="$node"})

panels.title: Services
panels.description: The services this platform depends on, and any other service that has failed.

panels.title: Kernel events since boot
panels.description: Counted from the kernel's own log. Xid is a GPU fault, AER a PCIe fault. link_down also happens when a peer reboots.

panels.title: Kernel events
panels.description: Per 10 minutes. Empty is the good case.
